talks.title: COVID 1984: Pandemic Propaganda and Surveillance
talks.teaser: Uncovers global propaganda campaigns, state surveillance initiatives, and disinformation networks deployed during the pandemic.
talks.summary:
Mauro Eldritch examines state surveillance, data harvesting, and propaganda campaigns deployed during the pandemic, focusing on an investigation into the Argentine government's mandatory contact tracing application, CUIDAR. He outlines how emergency public health measures were leveraged to normalize continuous location tracking, facial recognition, and personal data collection without adequate oversight.

Eldritch details the technical architecture and permissions required by the government tracking app at 01:52. He then investigates coordinated information operations on social media platforms at 03:50 and 05:54, exposing automated botnets and astroturfing campaigns designed to amplify pro-government messaging and suppress dissent. Using OSINT techniques and network graphing at 10:06 and 14:05, he maps how troll networks coordinate artificial trending topics and harass independent security researchers who disclose privacy vulnerabilities.

talks.title: Ambly: The Darknet Spider
talks.teaser: Introduces Ambly, an open-source dark web crawler and spider for mapping hidden Tor services and onion sites.
talks.summary:
In this Recon Village presentation, security researcher Levi introduces Ambly, an open-source web crawler and spider purpose-built for indexing and scraping hidden services on the Tor darknet network [00:00]. Levi outlines the unique architectural hurdles inherent to darknet reconnaissance, including high latency, unindexed hidden service directories, and the extreme volatility of onion sites that frequently appear and vanish without notice [07:23, 30:19].

Levi breaks down Ambly's modular software architecture, which interfaces with Tor through local SOCKS5 proxies to execute automated circuit rotation and distributed scraping [14:37, 22:13]. The crawler parses raw HTML, extracts referenced `.onion` URLs, strips metadata, and indexes text content into an isolated database while storing binary artifacts securely to protect analysts from malicious browser exploits [37:35]. He demonstrates how Ambly traverses community forums like Torum and Dread, following hyperlinks to uncover nested underground discussion boards and service listings [30:19].

The talk demonstrates how threat intelligence teams and red teams utilize Ambly to automate darknet surveillance. Levi showcases practical workflows for brand monitoring, tracking corporate credential leaks, identifying compromised employee access tokens, and mapping illicit marketplace supply chains across the dark web [37:35].

talks.title: COVID 1984: Propaganda and Surveillance in a Pandemic
talks.teaser: Deep dive into OSINT tracking of pandemic-era digital surveillance mechanisms, contact tracing apps, and propaganda.
talks.summary:
Mauro Eldritch presents an in-depth OSINT investigation into state-sponsored surveillance and digital propaganda deployed under the guise of emergency healthcare responses. Examining the Argentine national tracing ecosystem and its mandatory mobile application CUIDAR, he analyzes the risks of centralized location tracking, identity card binding, and unchecked data aggregation.

At 01:53, Eldritch breaks down application permissions, network telemetry, and background tracking mechanisms. He analyzes coordinated social media manipulation networks at 03:55 and 05:54, illustrating how automated bot farms and paid trolls execute swarm behavior to artificially influence public discourse. At 10:01 and 14:02, he showcases network topology analysis, sentiment manipulation metrics, and digital footprint tracking used to uncover the infrastructure supporting state-aligned information campaigns.

talks.title: Twitter Word Phrequency
talks.teaser: Demonstrates techniques and Python tooling for analyzing word frequencies, keyword trends, and linguistic patterns across Twitter data.
talks.summary:
Master Chen presents Twitter Word Phrequency, an open-source Python research project designed to perform natural language processing (NLP) and behavioral sentiment analysis on high-profile social media accounts [00:04]. Chen explains how open-source intelligence (OSINT) gathered from public social media feeds can reveal psychological profiles, communication habits, and ideological shifts [10:25].

The presentation covers the technical data collection and analysis pipeline built using Python, Twitter API scrapers, and Jupyter Notebooks [15:28]. Chen details the data normalization techniques required to process social media text, including tokenization, stop-word removal, and calculating n-gram word frequencies [20:54]. Using Donald Trump's public Twitter history as a primary case study, Chen demonstrates how tracking changes in lexical diversity, repetitive keyword spikes, and emotional terminology correlates with political market movements on platforms like PredictIt [05:13, 20:54].

Chen discusses data visualization techniques, showing how to transform raw frequency tables into intuitive word clouds, time-series frequency plots, and sentiment heatmaps [26:17]. He concludes with methodologies for adapting these scripts into active OSINT monitoring tools for social engineering assessments and threat intelligence profiling [31:23].
